subject: Performance / SLO follow-up — latency targets, streaming & cost levers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orchidhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Performance / SLO follow-up — latency targets, streaming & cost levers

Thanks again for the call earlier today — great conversation. I wanted to capture the key SLOs we talked through and propose next steps so we can size a short perf validation run. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary from today's discovery:
- Primary UX requirement: streaming token delivery for the assistant UI (render as tokens/partial responses arrive).
- Target latency: p95 end-to-end <= 250 ms for typical single-turn generation (user prompt -> first meaningful tokens).
- Typical response size: ~150 tokens on average; common follow-ups make sessions ~2 turns.
- Concurrency: steady 200 concurrent active sessions, with expected spikes up to ~400 for ~30–60s during peak batch notifications.
- Throughput: approximating 1.5k requests/min during peak sustained windows.

Key cost/perf levers we'll evaluate (attached quick reference):
- Continuous batching: reduce per-token overhead while maintaining sub-250ms p95 by limiting batch wait to X ms and using dynamic batching.
- KV / prefix caching: cache system prompts and repeated prefixes (you mentioned repeated patient-summary templates) to reduce compute.
- Quantization profiles: 8-bit or mixed-precision profiles that reduce GPU memory & cost vs 16-bit while preserving quality.
- Model variants / fallbacks: pick a smaller, faster variant for latency-sensitive paths and fall back to higher-fidelity variant for long tails.

Next steps I propose:
1) Short perf validation (2–4h): we run a Redwood-hosted test that mirrors your token distribution + spike profile. This will produce p50/p95/p99 latency and cost estimates under different configs.
2) We send a baseline config (batching, cache, quantization, model variant) — internal SE will confirm runtime knobs.
3) Align on target SLOs and acceptance criteria for the test.

Attachments: redwood-performance-levers.pdf (one‑pager), orchid-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposal).

If that looks right, I'll have Rishi schedule the perf run and share expected runtime config.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orchidhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchidhealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance / SLO follow-up — latency targets, streaming & cost levers

Thanks Marissa — adding a few technical clarifications so the perf test matches Orchid's real load:

Questions / clarifications:
- Tokenization: when you say ~150 tokens average, is that after deduping system prefix? (we often see a 30–70 token system prompt that can be cached)
- Streaming expectations: do you require server-sent events / chunked responses such that first byte is < 100ms, or is p95 for first 10 tokens acceptable?
- Quality tolerances: is occasional fall-back to a higher-precision model acceptable if the quantized variant has a small drop in ROUGE/QA checks?
- Spike profile: can you share the expected RPS curve (we'll simulate steady-state + 60s spike to 400 concurrency)?

Initial runtime knobs I'll test in the perf run:
- continuous_batching: target_max_latency_for_batch_ms = 12 (tunable)
- max_batch_size = 64 (controlled)
- kv_cache: enabled for system & user-prefixes (ttl 10m)
- quant_profile: 8-bit dynamic (we'll also test 16-bit float baseline)
- model_variants: rw-3-8q (low-latency), rw-3-16f (high-fidelity fallback)

I'll also capture both TTFB and total token completion times and produce cost projection per 1M tokens.

If you can confirm the tokenization and streaming detail, I'll stand up the perf harness and share timing for the run.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orchidhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance / SLO follow-up — latency targets, streaming & cost levers

Hi team — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers: 

- Tokenization: the 150-token number is total output tokens per response (we typically include a 64-token system + metadata prefix that repeats). So yes, prefix caching will help.
- Streaming: streaming is required. We need the UI to start rendering within 120ms for most flows; if first chunk < 120ms that's ideal. Sending first 10 tokens in that window is acceptable as long as they're delivered incrementally.
- Quality: we prefer model quality to be preserved; small regressions are acceptable for latency paths as long as we have a fallback to higher-fidelity for post-edit/longer generations.
- Spike curve: we'll export a short RPS curve from our telemetry — roughly 200 steady, spike to 400 for 45–60s once a day. We'll send the CSV in a follow-up.
- Budget: we're tracking to an average token-cost target; can you include projected cost per 1M output tokens for the configs you test?

Cc'ing Priya (platform) who will help run the footprint tests on our side if we need to run any hybrid tests.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director, Product Engineering | Orchid Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@orchidhealth.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance / SLO follow-up — latency targets, streaming & cost levers

Perfect — that's exactly the detail we need. Proposed plan + expected outputs: 

1) Run Redwood perf validation (2–4h): we'll replay your RPS curve (please send CSV) and the tokenizer distribution you mentioned (we'll use 64-token prefix + 150 token outputs). We'll capture: p50/p95/p99 TTFB, per-token tail latencies, and end-to-end completion times.

2) Configs to test (we'll produce 3 result rows):
   - Baseline: rw-3-16f, no quantization, batching minimal (for single-request latency baseline)
   - Latency-optimized: rw-3-8q, continuous batching (max wait 12ms, max_batch_size 64), KV prefix caching enabled
   - Hybrid: rw-3-8q primary + rw-3-16f fallback for offload/long tails; slightly larger batch windows for cost savings

3) Expected outcomes we will report back:
   - p95 TTFB and completion time for each config
   - Cost per 1M output tokens estimate (GPU time + infra overhead) per config
   - Recommendation on Dedicated vs Hosted: for consistent 200+ concurrency with predictable spikes, Dedicated capacity (reserved) or a dedicated pool gives best SLO guarantees; we'll quantify price delta vs hosted.

4) Next meeting: review results + agree on rollout (canary on a small percent of traffic).

I'll kick off the perf run once we get the RPS CSV. Rishi will own the run and share the results in a follow-up with graphs and the cost table.

Links: I've attached the mutual action plan and our performance levers one-pager for your platform team.

Best,
Marissa
